title.narrative: Output 3.2. Increased capacity of member States to formulate and implement policies and strategies for creating decent work in the rural economy

description.narrative:
The National Rural Employment Strategy (NRES) was approved at the Cabinet meeting and endorsed by the Prime Minister in September 2020. The Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare (MoLSW) led the drafting of the NRES through a highly consultative multi-stakeholder process with national and provincial authorities. The implementation in the Sekong and Savannakhet provinces was key to inform the subsequent NRES implementation at national level, expected from 2022. The implementation at local level applied approaches that created opportunities for self-employment and wage employment, mainly through public and private partnerships and cooperation among line agencies. Through better public extension services and private purchases, subsistence and food-insecure farming households transformed into champions, coffee farmers and forest pickers became successful vegetable and fruit cultivators. Young rural women were recruited into the economic zones through mobile employment services and training on industrial and soft skills combined with on-the-job training. In total, 561 households directly benefited from increased incomes of at least 30 per cent. Approximately 950 individuals participated (nearly 50 per cent female). Around 40 per cent are youth (35 years or less). In total, nearly $100,000 entered the target villages as revenues from new activities or higher production volume.
The interventions were found to be quite relevant in the context of the response to the COVID-19 pandemic, and this experience prepared the Office to respond to the need to support returning Lao migrants from Thailand. With the Swiss Development Cooperation support until December 2020 and ILO-Japan partnership funding support until June 2021, the ILO provided technical support to the development of the NRES. ILO also provided technical assistance and capacity development to national and provincial authorities of Sekong and Savannakhet and private sector to join forces in the implementation of the rural employment strategy.
